original_card.question: Does a new paid-profile or mixture-ceiling claim have independent source-bound coverage of its actual changed ledger?
methods: Independently reconstruct one changed paid ledger or pooled dual with exact source and model binding.
Check a genuinely uncovered moment implication with a different enclosure method and semantic controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Demonstrate independence, source binding, positive cases and semantic failure controls. Name the existing checks and the missing coverage. More digits or another equivalent evaluation of an unchanged root is not by itself new verification coverage.

first_step.inspect: Choose one uncovered implication in #4088 literal mixed fill, #4091 pooled dual/model binding or #4067 changed frame/host bill. #4091 pins an earlier #4088 head: validate word, capacity and stock equivalence before applying that ceiling to the later fill.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; no scientific replay, theorem acceptance or supplier admission. Budget any heavy replay separately.

original_card.first_experiment: Independently reconstruct one changed ledger or pooled certificate with a positive case and a semantic failure control. Compare exact sources and name what existing checks miss. Keep this separate from supplier-boundary-audit (ordinary/outer dispatch) and uniform-transfer-audit (all-size proof). Stop after the chosen implication; more digits of an unchanged root are not additional mechanism coverage.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Independent pricing prevents unsupported frontier claims and can reveal genuine accounting slack.
allowed_variations: Reconstruct either a source ledger or a numeric enclosure with a different method.
scope_change_triggers: Importing the primary function and calling its output independent verification.
Calling an aggregate histogram or source archive an independently accepted physical supplier.

actual_scope: Independently reconstruct the changed local ledger of PR #4629 (DaysSky, head 2cf7d081): the 213-helper re-padding, its paid/helper profiles, deficit, rank surplus at block 8 and block 7, and the invoice-to-complex-kappa price, from the written artifacts and main's PR4470 base word, without importing #4629's builder or verifier.
scope_change_reason: The card's examples (#4088/#4091/#4067) are historical; this applies the same question (independent coverage of a changed paid ledger) to the newest open complex-supplier ledger claim, #4629. Operator-level endpoint semantics (#4604) are only touched by one corroborating count.
bottleneck_link: #4629 claims the complex supplier rises 0.003020165977 -> 0.015637149091. Whether that ledger and its block-8 charge follow from the written word decides whether the complex side is still the binding constraint.
stop_rule: Stop after the re-padding ledger, the block-7/block-8 surplus and the kappa prices are independently recomputed with controls; do not attempt operator-level endpoint semantics or new constructions.
evidence: verify.py --replay: ledger and kappa 0.015637149091 reproduce; re-padding is +1 rank for 187 helpers and +5 for 26 (paid delta {1:187,5:26}), not one rank each; the ninth axis is reached only by these 213 helper final climbs (0 scalar/warp/centre events, 0 mains); the un-padded ledger prices higher (0.016571333483), so padding costs kappa; block-7 surplus is -256, not the stated -1,264; PR4470 itself has 326 cold full-ended helpers and fails the shipped 213 check that #4629 pads to satisfy. 5/5 rejection controls.

open_questions.question: Is the tensor block of a supplier word defined by its ambient dimension (ambient = block + 1), or fixed by the controller independently of the word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: #4629's admissibility rests on block 8; its word reaches the ninth axis only through 213 inert helper final climbs. Under the ambient rule without padding the ledger is block 7 (surplus -256, inadmissible); under a fixed-block rule the padding is unnecessary and the un-padded ledger prices 0.016571333483.
